# `nish/yaml-json`

One YAML document loaded into a `JsonDocument`, with every value's and key's source range, so that one validator and one `YamlLineIndex` serve a JSON text and a YAML text alike:

```ts
import {
  YAML_JSON_ERR_DEPTH,
  YAML_JSON_ERR_DOCUMENT,
  YAML_JSON_ERR_EXPANSION,
  YAML_JSON_ERR_MERGE,
  YAML_JSON_ERR_NOT_FINITE,
  YAML_JSON_ERR_NUMBER,
  YAML_JSON_ERR_YAML,
  YAML_JSON_MAX_RADIX_DIGITS,
  YAML_JSON_SCAN_KEYS,
  YamlJsonLoader,
  yamlJsonErrorName,
} from "nish/yaml-json";
```

```ts
import { parseYaml } from "nish/yaml"
import { JsonDocument, JsonLimits } from "nish/json-value"
import { YamlJsonLoader } from "nish/yaml-json"

const stream = parseYaml(text)
const doc = new JsonDocument(new JsonLimits())
const loader = new YamlJsonLoader()
const root = loader.load(stream, 0, doc)
// root < 0: loader.failed, loader.errorStart, loader.errorEnd
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="yamlJsonErrorName" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#yamljsonerrorname">

A `YAML_JSON_ERR_*` code's name, without the prefix; `""` for any other code.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="YamlJsonLoader" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#yamljsonloader">

Loads documents of a `YamlStream` into a `JsonDocument`.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

`load` clears the document and builds document `d` of the stream into it.
Every value's `start` and `end` are the byte range of the YAML node it came
from, as `YamlStream.start` and `end` give it (an anchor or a tag in front
is not included), and every key's `keyStart` and `keyEnd` the range of its
key node, quotes included. A key or value the text leaves out, the value of
`a:` or the key of `: b`, is an empty range at the end of its pair.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Scalars">

**Scalars** follow the core schema the stream resolves: null, booleans,
numbers and strings. A number is kept as JSON text, exactly: a `+` sign is
dropped, leading zeros are dropped, `.5` is `0.5` and `1.` is `1.0`, and a
`0x` or `0o` integer is written in decimal, however wide (up to
`YAML_JSON_MAX_RADIX_DIGITS` digits). `.inf`, `-.inf` and `.nan` have no
JSON spelling and are `YAML_JSON_ERR_NOT_FINITE`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Keys">

**Keys** are `keyText`'s: a string's decoded text, a number's or a
boolean's source text, `""` for null, a collection's flow text. Two YAML
keys that are different nodes can have the same text (`1` and `"1"`); the
second follows the document's `duplicates`, refused by default
(`JSON_VALUE_ERR_DUPLICATE`, at the second key) or holding the last value
under `JSON_VALUE_DUPLICATE_LAST`, as a parse of that JSON would.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Aliases are expanded">

**Aliases are expanded** into copies, and **merge keys** (`<<`, when the
stream was parsed with `merge`) are applied as `pathNode` reads them: the
map's own keys first, in order, then each merged map's keys it does not
already have, the first map listed winning, searched through its own merge
keys. A copied value keeps the ranges of the nodes it was copied from, so
an error inside it points at the anchored text, and the copy's root takes
the alias's range, where it is used.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**An alias bomb is refused before anything is built.** The values the
document expands to are counted first, from the nodes, with each node's
count kept, so the count costs one step per node however far the aliases
multiply it. Past the document's `maxValues` the load is
`YAML_JSON_ERR_EXPANSION`, at the first alias whose copy is the largest
(the first whose copy alone is past the limit, in a bomb), or
`JSON_VALUE_ERR_VALUES` when the document has no alias. A merged map counts
all its keys, also those the merging map overrides, so a document within a
few values of the limit can be refused for merges that would have fit.
The loader's merging is linear too: a map is merged into a given map at
most once, however many paths through the merge keys reach it, and the
pairs every merge visits and the items of every merge sequence it walks are
charged to a budget of `maxValues` plus the stream's node count, past which
the load is `YAML_JSON_ERR_EXPANSION` at the merge key. `parseYaml`'s own
merge check is not bounded this way: it walks a shared merge sequence once
for each merge key that names it.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="A merge key's value">

**A merge key's value** is a mapping, an alias to one, or a sequence of
those; anything else is refused at the value, by the parser as
`YAML_ERR_BAD_MERGE` (so `YAML_JSON_ERR_YAML`) and by the loader as
`YAML_JSON_ERR_MERGE`.
The text the copies store is bounded too, while they are built: past the
document's `JsonLimits.maxTotalBytes` of string, key and number text, the
load is `YAML_JSON_ERR_EXPANSION` at the outermost alias being copied, or
`JSON_TOK_ERR_TOTAL_LIMIT` at the node when no alias is.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Nesting">

**Nesting** is held to `maxDepth`, `JSON_WRITER_MAX_DEPTH` (64) by default,
counting copies, so that every loaded document can be written back as JSON;
deeper is `YAML_JSON_ERR_DEPTH`, at the node that is one too deep.

</scalar-detail>

A document with an error diagnostic is `YAML_JSON_ERR_YAML`, at the first
one's range, and loads nothing: a node the parser gave up on has no value
to load. Warnings are not errors.

A failed load clears the document and answers the code, which is also in
`failed`, with the range it is about in `errorStart` and `errorEnd`.
`yamlJsonErrorName` names a code. A map of `n` keys costs `O(n)` steps: the
loader finds repeated keys itself, with a hash map past
`YAML_JSON_SCAN_KEYS` keys, and adds each member through `JsonDocument`'s
internal `append`, where `set` would scan the members for every key it
adds. Every member it adds is a value it has just made, which is the
check `append` skips.

Every name here is `yamlJson`-prefixed, because a `std/` module is compiled
into the program that imports it and the symbol namespace is flat
(`std/README.md`). Every offset, count and code is an `i32`, and the module
runs under the Node prelude, where offsets count UTF-16 code units, as the
stream's do.

## YamlJsonLoader

Loads documents of a `YamlStream` into a `JsonDocument`. Keeps its scratch
from one load to the next. Its fields and its "Internal" methods are
reachable, as every member in Nish is; use `load` and the result fields.

```ts
class YamlJsonLoader
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new YamlJsonLoader()` |  |
| `bigAlias: i32` | Internal: the alias with the largest copy, and its size. |
| `bigSize: i32` |  |
| `byteCap: i32` |  |
| `cap: i32` | Internal: the most values the document may hold; a size saturates one past it. |
| `copying: i32` | Internal: the outermost alias being copied (`-1` for none), and the text the document may store. |
| `counted: i32[]` | Internal: the nodes the last count set a size on, the first `countedTop` of them: all a count clears. |
| `countedTop: i32` |  |
| `doc: JsonDocument` |  |
| `entryKeys: string[]` | Internal: the members of the maps being built, one map's after another's: each one's key text and pair, and the value node it holds (`-1` for none). |
| `entryPairs: i32[]` |  |
| `entryTop: i32` | Internal: where the next map member goes in the `entry` arrays. |
| `entryValues: i32[]` |  |
| `errorEnd: i32` |  |
| `errorStart: i32` | The byte range the error is about, and `-1` until one. |
| `failed: i32` | The last `load`'s code: `0`, a `YAML_JSON_ERR_*` code or a `JSON_VALUE_ERR_*` code. |
| `maxDepth: i32` | How deeply collections may nest, counting copies; `JSON_WRITER_MAX_DEPTH` so the result can be written. |
| `mergeBudget: i32` | Internal: the merged pairs the load may still visit. |
| `mergeMarks: i32[]` | Internal: per node, the stamp of the last map it was merged into; and that map's stamp. |
| `mergeStamp: i32` |  |
| `pending: i32[]` | Internal: the count's own stack of nodes. |
| `seen: Map<string, i32>` | Internal: a large map's key texts, to their entry. |
| `sizes: i32[]` | Internal: per node, the values it expands to (`0` not counted yet, `-1` being counted). |
| `stream: YamlStream` | Internal: the stream and document of the load in progress. |
| `addEntry(base: i32, pair: i32, own: boolean): i32` | Internal: adds pair `pair` to the entries of the map from `base`. A key already there is skipped for a merged pair; for an own pair it follows the document's `duplicates`, keeping the first key and its place. |
| `build(n: i32, depth: i32): JsonValue` | Internal: builds node `n`, nested `depth` collections deep, with `n`'s range on the value it answers. |
| `buildMap(at: i32, depth: i32): JsonValue` | Internal: a map's object. Its members are gathered first, own keys then merged ones, with repeats settled; then each value is built and added. |
| `buildScalar(at: i32): JsonValue` | Internal: a scalar's value, by its core-schema type. |
| `buildSeq(at: i32, depth: i32): JsonValue` | Internal: a sequence's array, each entry built in turn. |
| `count(root: i32, cap: i32): i32` | Internal: how many values node `root` expands to, saturating at `cap + 1`. Each node is counted once and its count kept, on a stack of its own rather than by recursion, because a chain of aliases can be as long as the text. Sets `bigAlias`. Clears only the sizes the last count set, so a stream of many documents is not cleared whole for each. |
| `fail(code: i32, start: i32, end: i32): i32` | Internal: records a failed load, clearing the document, and answers `code`. |
| `findEntry(base: i32, key: string): i32` | Internal: the entry from `base` whose key is `key`, or `-1`. The first `YAML_JSON_SCAN_KEYS` are compared one by one; the rest are in `seen`. |
| `isMergeKey(key: i32): boolean` | Internal: whether `key` is a merge key, as the stream reads one: a plain `<<`, untagged or `!!merge`. Keep in step with `yamlIsMergeKey` in `std/yaml.ts`, which is not exported. |
| `load(stream: YamlStream, d: i32, doc: JsonDocument): JsonValue` | Clears `doc` and loads document `d` of `stream` into it. Answers the root value, or a negative code, which is also in `failed`, with the range in `errorStart` and `errorEnd`; nothing is kept from a load that fails. |
| `markMerged(n: i32): boolean` | Internal: marks node `n` as merged into the current map; `false` if it already was. |
| `mergeInto(base: i32, at: i32, hops: i32): i32` | Internal: adds the merge keys' maps of map `at` to the entries from `base`, each key only if it is not there yet: every map a merge key names, in order, its own keys first and then its merge keys', `hops` deep. |
| `mergeMap(base: i32, pair: i32, m: i32, hops: i32): i32` | Internal: merges map `m`'s own keys, then its merge keys' maps, for the merge key `pair`; nothing if `m` is merged into this map already, since a second merge would find every key taken. |
| `newMergeStamp(): void` | Internal: starts a map's merges, so no node is marked as merged into it yet. |
| `nullAt(at: i32): JsonValue` | Internal: a null with the empty range at `at`. |
| `partSize(n: i32): i32` | Internal: a counted part's size: `1` for a missing node, too many for one still being counted. |
| `plus(a: i32, b: i32): i32` | Internal: `a + b`, saturating at `cap + 1`; both are at most that, so the sum fits. |
| `pushNode(top: i32, n: i32): i32` | Internal: pushes node `n` onto the count's stack unless it is counted; answers the new top. |
| `pushParts(top: i32, n: i32): i32` | Internal: pushes the nodes node `n`'s count is the sum of. |
| `ranged(v: JsonValue, start: i32, end: i32): JsonValue` | Internal: `v`, given the range `[start, end)`, or the failure the document answers. |
| `sizeOf(n: i32): i32` | Internal: node `n`'s count from its parts' counts, all of them kept by now; a part still being counted is a cycle, which counts as too many. |
| `tooMuchText(n: i32): i32` | Internal: the failure for text past `byteCap`, stored for node `n`. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="256" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_MAX_RADIX_DIGITS: i32`

The most digits a `0x` or `0o` integer may have, which is
`JSON_DEFAULT_MAX_NUMBER_BYTES`: writing one in decimal costs its digit count
times its decimal length, so a limit keeps a long one from costing the square
of the text.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="-44" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_ERR_DEPTH: i32`

Collections nest deeper than `maxDepth`, counting copies.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-40" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_ERR_DOCUMENT: i32`

Document `d` is not in the stream.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-43" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_ERR_EXPANSION: i32`

The aliases and merge keys expand the document past `maxValues`; the range is the first largest alias's.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-46" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_ERR_MERGE: i32`

A merge key's value is not a mapping or a sequence of mappings; the range is
the value's. `parseYaml` refuses these itself (`YAML_ERR_BAD_MERGE`, a load's
`YAML_JSON_ERR_YAML`); this is the loader's own check of the stream it is given.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-42" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_ERR_NOT_FINITE: i32`

`.inf`, `-.inf` or `.nan`, which JSON cannot spell.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-45" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_ERR_NUMBER: i32`

A `0x` or `0o` integer with more than `YAML_JSON_MAX_RADIX_DIGITS` digits.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-41" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_ERR_YAML: i32`

The document has an error diagnostic; the range is the first one's.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`YAML_JSON_SCAN_KEYS: i32`

Up to this many keys a map's keys are compared with each other; past it, through a hash map.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
